title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 47
paragraphs: They have worked this out because their land is suited to it and the rivers are their allies. First, the land is plain country, grassy and well watered, and the rivers flowing through it are not much fewer in number than the canals in Egypt. Of these, I will name those that are noteworthy and can be navigated from the sea: Ister with its five mouths; and after this, Tyras, Hypanis, Borysthenes, Panticapes, Hypakyris, Gerros, and Tanaïs. These flow as I shall now describe.
